newsitem.title: USA: Haitians protest outside New York police precinct.
newsitem.headline: Haitians protest outside New York police precinct.

text.p: Thousands of outraged protesters rallied outside a Brooklyn police precinct on Saturday demanding justice for the Haitian immigrant who said he was tortured and sodomized a week ago by police officers.

About 2,200 Haitian demonstrators including whites, Latinos and Jews, marched two miles from the nightclub where alleged victim Abner Louima was arrested to the 70th precinct station house where Louima said he was attacked with a toilet plunger.
Many of those who marched carried toilet plungers that they tossed into the air.
Despite chants of "No Justice, No Peace," and "KKK must go!" the noisy protesters were orderly, police said. "There have been no arrests," a police spokeswoman said.
The march began at 11 a.m. EDT and many of the protesters were still at the precinct at 7:30 p.m. EDT, despite sweltering temperatures and a rainstorm, police said.
Many in the crowd called for more arrests in addition to the two police officers Justin Volpe, 25, and Charles Schwarz, 31, named in an indictment on Friday.
The two officers were charged with aggravated sexual abuse and first degree assault. They face up to 25 years in prison if convicted. Both officers denied the charges.
"We are not anti-police. We are anti-police brutality," the Rev. Al Sharpton, a Democratic mayoral candidate told protesters.
Louima, 30, a night security guard, remains in critical condition in the intensive care unit at the Brooklyn Hospital Center with a tear to his colon, a lacerated bladder and abrasions to his mouth.
Protesters vowed to return daily to the police precinct until all of the officers involved in the alleged incidents were arrested.
